family: McMaster-Carr socket head cap screws (91290A series, black-oxide alloy steel, class 12.9) and hex nuts (90591A series, class 8, DIN 934)
title: 18 STEP files in vendor_cad/staging (SHCS-*.step, NUT-*.step); part numbers and pages from vendor_cad/staging/SOURCES.txt

screws_common.thread: modelled: a helical thread built from half-turn segments, from about 0.2 mm under the head to the tip on EVERY length (M3x30 and M5x35 included: fully threaded)
screws_common.socket: hex; M3 2.5 across flats, 1.5 deep; M5 4.0 across flats, 2.5 deep; M2.5 1.25 deep; M4 and M2.5 across-flats not resolved (socket not aligned with the file axes)
screws_common.head: plain cylinder with a small chamfer, no knurl

against_generated_iso_solids.screws: head diameter, head height, thread diameter, length and socket size equal the ISO 4762 values in iso_fasteners.json on every file. The generated detail head is the knurled maximum (5.68 for M3, 8.72 for M5); McMaster's is the plain 5.5 / 8.5, the same as the simulation solid
against_generated_iso_solids.nuts: M2.5 and M3 equal ISO 4032 (5.0 x 2.0, 5.5 x 2.4). **M5 differs: 4.0 mm thick (DIN 934) against 4.7 mm (ISO 4032) in the catalogue**; across flats 8.0 both

cost.mcmaster_M3x30: 767 faces, 22,144 triangles at 0.1 mm (64,872 at 0.02 mm), 3.9 MB STEP, 5 s to read
cost.estimate_all_mcmaster: about 1.7 million triangles for v6's screws and nuts, against about 0.15 million generated (printer_v4's whole viewer export is 0.27 million)

against_generated_iso_solids.recommendation: (c) keep the generated ISO solids as simulation and detail models; record the McMaster part numbers and these dimensions. Consider (b), a defeatured copy with the thread replaced by a cylinder, only if a close-up render ever needs the real head
